6db5ef2f616a3817: HONG KONG: New World Development said on Tuesday it has asked bondholders to swap some of its debt due in 2027 and 2028 for new notes maturing in 2032, as the Hong Kong developer seeks to extend its repayment schedule and improve liquidity.
The company said a newly established unit plans to issue up to US$600 million of new 7.375 per cent secured notes due 2032 in exchange for existing notes.
7f9c6f6b8a0b23c4: LAGOS: A Nigerian Air Force plane crashed on Monday in the country's southwest, killing all 32 people on board, President Bola Tinubu said, declaring three days of national mourning.
It is one the worst air disasters in recent years in Africa's most populous country.

The passenger aircraft was on a "routine mission" from Benin City in southern Nigeria to the economic hub of Lagos when it went down at Igbokoda in southwestern Ondo state shortly after 9am (0800 GMT), the president and the air force said.
"The president extends his deepest condolences to the family of the 25 passengers and seven crew members involved," Tinubu's office said in a statement.
"This is a painful moment for our armed forces and for the entire nation," he said.
Tinubu's spokesman Bayo Onanuga said in a later statement that the president "has declared a three-day national mourning for Air Force personnel who died in the crash."
He also directed that flags be flown at half-staff across the country to pay respect to the officers.
The Air Force will release the identities of the victims after notifying their families, the presidency said.
The plane crashed near a naval base, according to the presidency and the Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo.
Both described it as an ATR-42 – a twin-engine turboprop that the manufacturers say can carry between 30 and 50 passengers
A video circulating on social media showed a small crowd gathered near a river while rescuers searched the area by boat.
The president said he had "directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences."

Dayo Akinte, 39, a firewood hawker who lives about a kilometre from where the accident occurred, described to AFP hearing a sound she thought was "thunder" at the time she believed the plane went down.
Since the crash, "three aircraft have also been flying over the scene", she said by phone.
She said someone who went fishing in the swamp alerted the nearby naval base and people in the town about the crash.
Airforce spokesman Ehimen Ejodame earlier said "search and rescue operations" were ongoing "in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies."
Police also confirmed the accident but provided no details.
Igbokoda is located in Ilaje, an oil-producing region in southern Nigeria.

In May 2021, Nigeria's top-ranking army commander, Lieutenant General Ibrahim Attahiru, and 10 other officers were killed when their plane crashed in bad weather while trying to land at northern Kaduna state airport.
Seven people died when a military plane crashed into a house in northern Nigeria killing everyone on board in August 2015.
Earlier that same month, a helicopter crashed into a lagoon in Lagos, killing six, including the American pilot.

2c49067fbfca922a: NEW YORK, Oct 6 — Leading artificial intelligence companies do not know how to keep AI systems from pursuing objectives their developers did not assign, whistleblower Jacob Coxon, a former OpenAI and Anthropic employee, warned Monday.
“Companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes,” Coxon told local lawmakers at a hearing before the New York City Council.

In early September, the British researcher published a statement on X explaining his decision to resign from Anthropic, saying AI developers sincerely believed the technology could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”
His testimony made headlines around the world, and several current and former employees of AI’s major players have since voiced similar concerns.

While AI could bring “tremendous benefits” to society, “on the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control of these AIs and could end in human extinction,” he said Monday.
“We don’t know how to prevent them from developing goals of their own,” beyond their creators’ control, Coxon explained, “and we don’t have the safeguards to prevent them from acting on these goals.”
The Cambridge University graduate took aim at tech industry culture, saying companies “run on a startup mindset: move fast, break things, fix them later.”
“That works for a photo sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever,” Coxon said.

“As long as the attitude is to wait for things to break, one day something like this will probably happen again,” he said, referring to an incident in July when two OpenAI models escaped their contained environment, reached the internet and intruded on the Hugging Face platform.
“Except the AIs will be much more capable,” he added.

“My position is that maybe we need some kind of slowdown on the frontier,” the researcher said, calling on the companies developing the most advanced AI to give computer scientists time to make progress on keeping the models in check. — AFP
88f8e252e5473f45: OCTOBER 6 — One of the most familiar experiences in microbusiness is having a business that looks busy while the owner continues worrying about money. Orders are coming in, parcels are waiting to be shipped and customers are active during live-selling sessions. Then the end of the month arrives.

Suppliers need to be paid. Packaging needs to be reordered. Advertising has already taken part of the revenue. Some products were sold at a discount, while new stock needs to be purchased. Suddenly, a month that looked very busy no longer feels particularly profitable.

This is one of the lessons that comes with experience. Sales do not necessarily mean that a business is financially strong. Money can constantly move in and out, with little actually remaining in the business.

This everyday reality is part of an important aspect of Malaysia’s economy. According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), MSMEs contributed 39.7% of Malaysia’s GDP in 2025. Behind that large national figure, however, are individual business owners making much smaller but important decisions every day: how much stock to buy, whether to spend more on advertising, or whether to keep the money available today for next month.
For the entrepreneur, these are not abstract business decisions. A wrong decision can remain visible for months as boxes that still need to be sold.
When we become very good at surviving

After several years, entrepreneurs develop instincts that are difficult for outsiders to see. When sales fall, they know which expenses to reduce first. When stock moves slowly, they know how to clear it. When a supplier becomes unreliable, they know who else to contact.

This ability to adapt, reorganise limited resources and continue operating during uncertain conditions is closely related to what I have described as Entrepreneurial Survival Capability (ESC). Such capability does not develop overnight. It accumulates through weak sales months, failed products, supplier problems, rising costs and the many decisions that have to be made when circumstances become difficult.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The author argues that entrepreneurial success should not be measured by survival alone, but by whether experience helps a business recover, strengthen and grow beyond constant struggle. — Pexels pic

But there is something we discuss much less often: an entrepreneur can become very good at surviving. She knows how to solve this month’s problem. Another problem arrives next month, and she finds a way through that too. Year after year, the business remains open. Yet the business may still be standing in almost the same place.
What saved the business does not always need to stay

Imagine a business owner who once suffered a significant loss after ordering too much stock. Afterward, she becomes extremely cautious. She buys smaller quantities and chooses safer colours. At the time, this strategy may have protected her cash flow.

Several years later, demand is stronger, but popular products repeatedly run out because she is still afraid of holding too much stock. A difficult experience from the past continues to shape decisions in a business that is now operating under different conditions.

The same can happen when an owner has a disappointing experience with an employee and decides it is easier to do everything herself. Initially, the decision saves money. Years later, she may still be photographing products, replying to messages, conducting live sessions, checking payments and packing parcels alone late at night.

Those strategies were not necessarily wrong. They may have been exactly what the business needed at the time. The difficulty arises when a temporary survival response becomes a permanent way of operating.
This is where experience needs to do more than remind us of previous mistakes. Experience becomes capability when lessons from the past improve future decisions.
Recovery is progress too

When sales become stable again, the natural temptation may be to think about growth: buy more stock, introduce another product, increase advertising or enter another sales channel. But a business that has just been through a difficult period may not be ready to grow. It may need to recover first.

Recovery could mean replacing the personal savings used during difficult months, clearing old inventory, rebuilding working capital or creating enough financial reserve so that one slow month does not immediately become an emergency. These achievements are not particularly exciting to display on social media. Yet they make the business less fragile.

Survival keeps the business alive. Recovery allows it to regain its strength. An entrepreneur who is rebuilding should therefore not assume that she is falling behind simply because the business is not expanding quickly. Sometimes rebuilding what was lost is exactly the progress the business needs.
Has the business grown, or has the owner simply become busier?
Another familiar phrase among microbusiness owners is, “Better I do it myself.”

At the beginning, it makes sense. Doing things personally saves money. But when five orders become twenty, and twenty become fifty, the owner’s workload increases too. Sales increase, but so do the hours she works.
This creates an important question: has the business actually grown, or has the entrepreneur simply become busier?

Growth does not necessarily mean opening ten outlets. For a microbusiness, it could mean better inventory management, more repeat customers, additional help during busy periods, or the ability to take a day off without the entire operation stopping. Sometimes growth means making the business stronger, not simply bigger. This matters because remaining small is not the same as remaining fragile.
Still standing, but what comes next?

There is something meaningful about an entrepreneur looking back after eight or ten years and saying, “I am still here.” Behind those words may be unsold stock, difficult customers, rising costs, supplier problems and countless decisions that only became obviously right or wrong after the money had already been spent. All those experiences have value. The ability to survive has value too.

But we should be careful not to romanticise permanent struggle as entrepreneurial success. Working longer every year simply to remain in approximately the same position does not necessarily mean the business is becoming stronger. Being busy is not always the same as making progress.

Farah may still be packing orders tonight after everyone else in the house has gone to bed. There may be a few boxes of slow-moving hijabs beside her, along with another message from a supplier waiting to be read. Tomorrow, she will probably wake up and do what years in business have taught her to do: find a way to keep going.
She may never describe herself as a resilient entrepreneur. She may never use the phrase “Entrepreneurial Survival Capability.”
She may simply say, “Business memang macam ni. Ada masa okay, ada masa susah.”
But after years of navigating the ups and downs of business, perhaps the question is no longer whether she knows how to survive. She has already demonstrated that capability many times.
The next question is how everything she has experienced can help strengthen the business.
Because survival keeps the business alive. Recovery restores its strength. And growth creates the space to build what comes next.
* The author is a Research Fellow Post Doctorate at the Ungku Aziz Centre for Development Studies (UAC), Universiti Malaya, and can be reached at nikzirwatul@um.edu.my
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
f35fbb6369fa0583: NEW YORK: L'Oreal has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

The cosmetics maker's US unit is working with restructuring counsel Weil Gotshal & Manges and investment bank Ducera Partners to address lawsuits from individuals alleging the talc products caused illness, the Journal said, citing people familiar with the matter.

L'Oreal said in its latest half-year report that about 760 US proceedings over the alleged presence of asbestos particles in some talc-containing cosmetic products were pending as of June 30, up from about 620 at the end of 2025, and that it strongly contests the claims.

The Journal said L'Oreal is considering moving tort liabilities into a separate corporate entity to unload them through a sale to an outside investor, allowing the company to separate its exposure from its operating businesses.

As an option to address the claims outside Chapter 11, L'Oreal's advisers are exploring a sale similar to Honeywell's divestiture last year of certain asbestos liabilities to corporate liability acquisition platform Delticus, the Journal said.
L'Oreal, Weil Gotshal & Manges and Ducera did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

More broadly, talc litigation has cost Johnson & Johnson billions of dollars in a legal fight lasting more than a decade and has prompted several companies to try to resolve claims in bankruptcy court.

In July, J&J said it would pay an estimated US$5.5 billion to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging its baby powder and other talc products cause ovarian cancer. It had earlier filed for three bankruptcies through a shell-company subsidiary in an effort to settle the cases, though each ended in dismissal.
Avon Products, a US-based holding company of the Avon beauty brand, started Chapter 11 proceedings in 2024 to address its debt and talc liabilities.

L'Oreal is also facing thousands of lawsuits alleging its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women. Arizona sued L'Oreal and its US subsidiary in September, alleging the cosmetics company hid evidence that the products could cause cancer.
L'Oreal USA has previously said the company is confident in the safety of its products and believes those claims are without legal or scientific merit.

1be1a53263ce4b8b: KOTA BARU: Police are identifying a man believed to be linked to the vandalism of Al-Aziz Al-Hadi Mosque in Kota SPP Warisan, Tumpat, yesterday.
Tumpat police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairi Shafie said CCTV footage from the mosque showed a man believed to be connected to the incident, which occurred at 6.35am.

He said police received a report from a member of the public, while initial checks found that the mosque's glass door had been smashed and a foul-smelling, greenish-brown liquid poured onto the carpet in the prayer hall.
"The case is being investigated under Sections 295 and 427 of the Penal Code," he said in a statement last night.
Khairi said police were also investigating the motive and assessing the extent of the damage and losses incurred.

He urged the public not to speculate, make accusations or spread unverified information, and advised anyone with information to contact the Tumpat district police headquarters operations room at 09-725 6226.
ce170da435f06724: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The presence of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia and student safety in schools are expected to be among the issues raised at today’s Dewan Rakyat sitting.

According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, during the Minister’s Question Time, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) will ask the Prime Minister to outline the government’s steps to address the long-standing presence of Myanmar nationals, including refugees and asylum seekers, which has raised public concern.

Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) will ask the Prime Minister why incidents threatening student safety continue in schools despite government safety guidelines and procedures being in place.

During the Question and Answer session, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) will ask the Home Minister for the latest status on implementing 17 recommendations to strengthen security controls, screening, and risk management at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and other international gateways in the country.

The cross-border haze issue is also among the matters likely to be raised in the lower house of Parliament, with Datuk Yusuf Abd Wahab (GPS-Tanjong Manis) scheduled to ask the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister about steps taken to address the problem, particularly in Sarawak.
He will also seek information on diplomatic or legal actions the ministry has taken to address the ongoing haze issue.

Following the Question and Answer session, the sitting will proceed with the first reading of the Supply Bill 2027 by the Finance Minister and the second reading of the Sports Development (Amendment) Bill 2026 by the Youth and Sports Minister.
The Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament for the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to sit for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama
61303012caddad43: NEW YORK: New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a US state since cases began surging in 2025.
The state also expanded the pool of health professionals allowed to administer measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccines as cases rise in rural communities.
"No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease," Hochul said in a statement.

New York has reported 108 measles cases this year through Oct 3, including 92 since July 15 in under-immunised rural communities across 18 counties, well above typical annual levels, according to the executive order.

Seven of the cases are in New York City, and 101 are elsewhere in the state, the governor's office said. Local health departments have administered more than 1,000 MMR doses in rural areas since July 15.
Neighbouring Pennsylvania is battling a fast-spreading outbreak, with 977 cases and five deaths as of Oct 2, mostly in rural counties that border New York, the order said.
Pennsylvania health officials said on Monday the state's total had passed 1,000 cases, making it the largest state outbreak in more than three decades.
The US is having its worst year for measles since 1991, with nearly 3,900 cases reported, according to the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.
The order allows registered nurses to order tests for suspected measles and pharmacists to vaccinate children as young as two.
It also requires all MMR vaccinations to be reported to state or New York City immunisation registries within 72 hours, while waiving adults' consent for such reporting.
Vaccination itself still requires the consent of the patient or a legal guardian. The emergency took effect on Monday and runs through Nov 4.
b7b23fe658cd3eed: NEW YORK: Data centre operator DayOne Data Centers filed for an initial public offering in the United States on Monday, testing investor appetite for data-center listings amid challenging market conditions.
The company posted a net loss of US$77.2 million on revenue of US$512 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a loss of US$12.6 million on revenue of US$151.5 million a year earlier.
The filing comes as surging bond yields and elevated interest rates cloud the outlook for the fall IPO market, prompting several major listings to be postponed.
Data centres have also come under scrutiny over their heavy use of electricity, water and land, with communities raising concerns about their impact on power grids, utility bills and local resources.
The Singapore-based company develops and operates data centres for cloud-computing and AI customers, providing space, power, cooling and connectivity, primarily under long-term contracts.
DayOne operates across Asia-Pacific and Europe, including Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain, according to its filing.
Shanghai-based GDS Holdings set up GDS International in Singapore in 2022, which was rebranded as DayOne in January 2025 following its separation from the parent company.
The company has not disclosed the size of the offering, although Reuters reported in February that it was aiming to raise as much as US$5 billion at a potential valuation of US$20 billion.
DayOne plans to use the IPO proceeds to develop and construct new data centre projects and for working capital and other general corporate purposes.
Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, BofA Securities and Citigroup are among the underwriters for the offering. DayOne plans to list its American depositary shares on the Nasdaq under the symbol "DODC".
4431e1938fbbf297: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Zetrix AI Berhad has submitted a proposal to the Malaysian government to address outstanding remittances after authorities suspended its Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection services over RM314 million in unpaid government revenue.

The technology company said in a statement yesterday that resolving the outstanding obligations was its immediate priority, while efforts to restore the affected services would be subject to the relevant approvals.
“Zetrix AI has submitted a proposed solution to the Government of Malaysia to address the outstanding remittances for their consideration,” it said.
“The Group’s immediate priority is to resolve these obligations and work towards restoring the affected services, subject to the relevant approvals.”
The company did not disclose details of the proposed solution.

Transport Minister Anthony Loke said yesterday that My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI, both under the MYEG Group, had failed to remit RM314 million in government revenue collected between May 19 and September 30.

He said the authorities had issued 35 reminders and engaged the companies since May in an attempt to recover the outstanding funds before their services as government revenue collection agents were suspended.
Loke said MYEG had also issued a cheque for RM231 million dated September 30, but the payment could not be processed by the bank following instructions from the company.

“Therefore, the Ministry of Transport and the Road Transport Department had to take the drastic step of suspending payment services through MyEG and Zetrix AI from today,” he said at a press conference yesterday.
The ministry and JPJ will also initiate legal action to recover the full RM314 million, Loke said.
Zetrix AI, meanwhile, expressed regret over the inconvenience caused by the suspension, which took effect on October 5.
“As a provider of JPJ services since 2000, we understand the importance of ensuring these essential services remain accessible, reliable and convenient for the public,” it said.
“The Group recognises its responsibility to customers and remains committed to fulfilling its obligations to the Government.”
The company also assured customers who had used the affected JPJ services before the suspension that their transactions had already been processed and fulfilled.
Loke said the suspension would not disrupt JPJ services more broadly, with transactions still available through alternatives including the MyJPJ app, JPJ Public Portal, counters and kiosks.

JPJ had announced on October 2 that services provided by MyEG and Zetrix AI as collection agents would be suspended from 12.01am on October 5 following non-compliance with the terms of their agreements.

Zetrix AI, formerly known as MY E.G. Services Berhad, began operations in 2000 as a provider of electronic government services and has since expanded into blockchain and artificial intelligence services.
ed56b902ab840d53: NEW YORK: Oil prices down on Tuesday as resilient Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concerns, though attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi targets kept traders wary of risks to Gulf supplies.
Brent crude futures lost four cents to US$100.28 a barrel by 0003 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 11 cents, or 0.1 per cent, to US$89.33 a barrel.
"Oil is little changed after yesterday's decline as traders continue to digest a modest easing in supply-side anxiety," said KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer.
"The pickup in Saudi export numbers and the G7 decision to release strategic reserves are helping keep a lid on prices for now, even while Brent remains anchored around the US$100 level," he said.

Crude exports from the Middle East exceeded pre-war levels on four days during the last week of September, shipping data showed on Monday, underscoring the resilience of regional oil flows despite attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Further easing supply concerns, G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions after pressure from US President Donald Trump.

However, the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen continued to fuel concerns over potential disruptions to supply from the region's largest oil exporter amid a stalemate in US-Iran talks.

Yemen's Houthis said on Monday they had carried out attacks on several sites in Saudi Arabia, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and Abha airport. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation.
Without a clear diplomatic breakthrough or a further material improvement in export efficiency, the floor under prices looks reasonably firm, Waterer said.
ab94775dc35cc53e: LONDON, Oct 6 — British author Jeffrey Archer, who penned a series of best-selling novels, served as a Conservative MP and was convicted of perjury, died suddenly at 86, his publisher HarperCollins said.
Archer died “suddenly and peacefully at his home between writing sessions” on Monday, HarperCollins said.
His editor, Kate Elton, called him a “master storyteller and an editor’s dream”.
The writer had been due to appear at Cheltenham Literary Festival this week to discuss “Adam and Eve”, what he described as his final novel after 50 years of storytelling.
It was due to be published Tuesday.
The Sun tabloid reported that he had been signing books for fans at an event in London on Sunday.
Archer had revealed in 2014 that he had been diagnosed with prostate cancer.
The author led a life as colourful as the characters in his novels, which sold over 300 million copies, according to his website.
Talented and ambitious, he was a high flyer who could never quite escape the whiff of scandal despite a talent for bouncing back from humiliating setbacks.
Politics and sex were the ingredients which ensured his success as a novelist.
But in real life the combination led to the downfall of the man who once hoped to become mayor of London.
He was tried for perjury and perverting the course of justice after a friend admitted he had supplied a false alibi during a libel case the peer brought against the Daily Star tabloid in 1987.
Archer had sued the newspaper over a claim he had slept with a prostitute, winning £500,000 in damages.
Ambitious from his earliest years, Archer used his charm and fund-raising abilities to climb almost to the top of the Conservative Party.
MP at 29
He joined the Tories while a student at Britain’s prestigious Oxford University and in 1969 won a resounding by-election victory to become a member of parliament at the age of 29.
His parliamentary career came to an abrupt end in 1974 when he was brought to the brink of bankruptcy by the collapse of a Canadian industrial cleaning company in which he had invested.

However, with typical resilience he used his experiences as material for his first book “Not A Penny More, Not A Penny Less”, published in 1975, the first of a series of blockbusters set in the worlds of high finance and politics.
Panned by the critics, they nevertheless earned him a fortune and Archer nursed hopes of a political revival while using his contacts and persuasiveness to raise millions of pounds for the Tories.
In 1985, his labours were recognised by then prime minister Margaret Thatcher, who named him Conservative deputy chairman, describing him as a model Tory high achiever.
Scandals
But a year after his appointment, he was forced to resign by what he described as a “lack of judgment” after sending £2,000 to a prostitute, Monica Coghlan.
He maintained he only paid the money to help her escape hounding from reporters by going abroad and sued the Daily Star for suggesting otherwise.
In 1992 he was recommended by Thatcher’s successor John Major for a peerage, entitling him to sit in the House of Lords, the upper chamber of parliament.
In 1999, he launched a campaign to become the Tory party’s candidate to become the first elected mayor of London.

But months later the claim emerged that he had asked a friend, Ted Francis to provide him with a false alibi against the Daily Star. This forced him to abandon his bid and he was expelled from the party.
In 2001 he went on trial and was found guilty of perjury and perverting the course of justice. He was sentenced to four years in prison, but was granted parole in 2003.
Archer’s long-suffering wife Mary, a scientist, stood behind her husband in his many mishaps.
Famously praised for her “fragrance” by the judge in the 1987 libel trial, she once said: “We’ve explored the further reaches of ‘for better and for worse’ than most couples.”
Archer retired from the House of Lords in 2024. His wife is Chancellor of the University of Buckingham. — AFP
1837b44ca39ce592: NEW YORK: The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports.
It was the Nasdaq's second day of sharp gains after weaker-than-expected jobs data on Friday dampened expectations for an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting this month.
The S&P 500 rose and was about 0.3 per cent below its August 13 record high close.
AI heavyweight Nvidia climbed 2.1 per cent and also reached a record-high close, boosting its stock market value to US$5.76 trillion.
Microsoft added 1.5 per cent, while Meta Platforms and Tesla gained about two per cent each.
Oil prices slipped after crude exports from the Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies.

"With the economic data calendar being light and earnings about a week away, investors are really groping for anything positive to glom onto, and clearly they're looking at lower energy prices," said Art Hogan, chief ​market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.
BANKS KICK OFF THIRD-QUARTER RESULTS
Third-quarter earnings season kicks off next week with reports from large US banks.
Analysts on average see S&P 500 earnings jumping over 30 per cent year over year, thanks largely to AI-related stocks, according to LSEG data.

Following jobs data on Friday that showed US job growth slowed more than expected in September, traders see a 24 per cent chance of an interest rate hike at the Fed's October meeting, down from a 70 per cent chance a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
PTC surged 33 per cent after France's Schneider Electric agreed to acquire the software firm in a US$22.6 billion all-cash deal.
The S&P 500 climbed 0.66 per cent to end the session at 7,773.95 points.
The Nasdaq gained 1.05 per cent to 27,477.31 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.18 per cent to 51,267.90 points.
The Nasdaq's previous record high close was on September 22.
Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by materials , up 1.22 per cent, followed by a 1.14 per cent gain in communication services.
Optimism about robust corporate earnings has helped US stocks outperform global rivals in the last six months, despite rising Treasury yields and higher oil prices related to the US war with Iran.

RXO jumped over 22 per cent after logistics firm C.H. Robinson Worldwide agreed to buy the transportation broker in a stock-and-cash transaction for US$5.8 billion. C.H. Robinson fell nearly 11 per cent.

Cerebras Systems rose 9 per cent after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on social media the chip designer is a "close partner" and that the companies have "deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed."
Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 by a 1.7-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 13 new highs and 20 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 57 new highs and 243 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was relatively light, with 16.8 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.3 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

c973344f3a1412f8: GEORGE TOWN: Rapid Penang has begun a two-day trial of electric buses as part of preparations to introduce low-carbon public transport in the state.

The trial follows similar sessions by Rapid KL and forms part of Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd's efforts to replace its existing fleet with safer, more sustainable vehicles while improving operational efficiency.
Two electric buses from different manufacturers — a 12-metre Foton bus and an 8.25-metre Golden Dragon bus — will be tested on selected routes to assess their real-world suitability.
The evaluation will focus on route compatibility, traffic performance, energy consumption, charging efficiency, safety, and passenger comfort.
Rapid Bus chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the trial marks a crucial step toward launching Penang's first electric buses.

"It is an important benchmark to ensure the operations team has sufficient data and experience to assess the performance, capabilities and operational requirements of electric buses under actual conditions before they are introduced on existing routes," he said.
Rapid Penang is also establishing essential support infrastructure, including charging and maintenance facilities, staff training, and operational frameworks.
Electric buses will be introduced in stages following the trial, with Rapid Penang continuing to refine operational readiness to ensure smooth service for commuters.
The operator is currently in the first phase of procuring 75 electric buses, with deliveries scheduled in stages through March 2027.
The procurement forms part of a wider bus replacement programme in Penang involving 240 electric buses and 70 new diesel buses.

The initiative aligns with the National Energy Transition Roadmap, the National Transport Policy 2019-2030, the Penang Transport Master Plan, and the Penang Green Agenda, which aims to make Penang Malaysia's greenest state by 2030.
The initiative is also aligned with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and National Transport Policy 2019-2030, while supporting Penang's efforts to promote sustainable urban mobility.
e4c669ce80d871da: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is looking to gradually reduce its reliance on the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) as its capacity to manage refugees and asylum seekers improves.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the move was part of a review of the UNHCR office's operations, scope and functions in Malaysia.
He said the review was being undertaken in line with the implementation of the Refugee Registration Document (DPP), which is aimed at strengthening Malaysia's own refugee management mechanism.

"The government is currently reviewing the direction of the operations of the UNHCR office in Malaysia, including the scope of its role and functions, so that they are aligned with the implementation of the DPP and government-led national mechanisms.

"In the long term, this direction also takes into account the gradual reduction of dependence on UNHCR, in line with the increasing capacity of the government to take over the management of refugees and asylum seekers," he said in a parliamentary written reply.

Mohamad was responding to Datuk Seri Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran), who asked about the legal basis and government decisions allowing UNHCR to operate in Malaysia despite the country not being a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol.
Ronald also asked about the scope of UNHCR's functions, powers and responsibilities agreed to by the government.

Mohamad said the DPP was being implemented under National Security Council Directive No. 23 (2023 revision) to strengthen the management of refugees and asylum seekers, including through data coordination, identity verification, monitoring and regulation.
The mechanism would also reduce reliance on records held by foreign entities, he said.
Mohamad said Malaysia was not a party to the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees or its 1967 Protocol.

However, on humanitarian grounds, the government had allowed refugees and asylum seekers to remain temporarily in the country until they were resettled in third countries or returned to their countries of origin.
He said the UNHCR office had operated in Malaysia since 1975, adding that its presence and operations did not alter Malaysia's position as a non-signatory to the convention.
"UNHCR's mandate is limited to providing protection and assistance to refugees," he said.

In the context of refugee and asylum seeker management in Malaysia, Mohamad said UNHCR's functions included registration and documentation, refugee status determination and resettlement to third countries.
All UNHCR cardholders remained subject to Malaysian laws, he added.
ddab1f8f3b8ab20c: KUALA LUMPUR: Pahang is positioning itself for a major economic transformation through the development of Pahang Aerospace City (PAC), a 4,856.23-hectare integrated hub expected to generate between RM30 billion and RM40 billion in development value over the next 15 years.

Pahang State Investment, Industrial Development, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Datuk Seri Mohamad Najib said PAC would broaden the state's economic base beyond its traditional industries by attracting investments in aerospace, space, artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced mobility.
"This means Pahang is expanding its economic base into new industries," he told Business Times.
Nizar said the development would be anchored by a new international airport, but would extend well beyond aviation to create an integrated ecosystem of industrial and economic activities.
"Generally, based on the size of the PAC development, the development value should be around RM30 billion to RM40 billion over a span of 15 years," he said.
He said the new airport would form part of a wider development spanning about 4,856.23 hectares, with multiple industry clusters planned across the site.
"It is not limited to airport development alone. We have many other interesting development components that will be developed in the area," he said.

Nizar said these included aerospace and aeronautics industries, maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), AI-powered data centres, drones, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and a Space City.

He said the proposed international airport alone was expected to have a gross development cost of between RM1.2 billion and RM1.6 billion and would be designed to cater to two million passengers annually.
"The airport will be an international airport under ICAO Category 4C, with a runway of 4.1 kilometres and a width of 67 metres.

"We are designing the airport to cater for all types of narrow-body aircraft, particularly those commonly operated in Asean, while it will also be able to cater for wide-body aircraft operations," he said.
He said the airport would also support cargo-related operations, including connectivity with Kuantan Port, while providing greater capacity compared with the existing airport.
Nizar said the new airport was necessary, as the existing Sultan Ahmad Shah Airport had limited flight operations due to shared airspace with the Royal Malaysian Air Force.
"The existing airport is limited because we share the airspace with the Royal Malaysian Air Force, so flight operations are very limited.
"If we move to this site, we will have more space for international aviation, and it will become an international-status airport," he said.
The new airport is targeted to begin operations in the fourth quarter of 2031, although other components of PAC are expected to be developed and operationalised earlier.
Nizar said development would be implemented in parallel across three broad phases, rather than sequentially, with some components expected to begin operating as early as 2027.
"The main timeline is the airport, which is expected to operate in the fourth quarter of 2031. But not everything will be completed at that time.
"We expect around 60 to 70 per cent of the development to be completed by around 2035," he said.
CHERATING GATEWAY TO TAP ECRL, DATA CENTRE POTENTIAL
Nizar said the transit-oriented development (TOD), known as the Cherating Gateway, would be among the first components to move forward, with activities expected to begin in February 2027.
He said the TOD would be directly connected to the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) station and was intended to stimulate economic and social activity around the railway connection.
"Cherating Gateway is actually more orientated towards TOD and the economic accelerator programme, which is tied to the development of the East Coast Rail Link.
"The function of Cherating Gateway is that from the ECRL route, we will stimulate the economy, social activities and commercial activities in the area," he said.
Nizar said the Cherating Gateway would include a motorsports complex, commercial and shopping components, a convention centre, residential development and a data centre precinct.
He said about 161.87 hectares had been allocated for data centre operators, with several operators currently conducting feasibility studies.
"The advantage of PAC and the TOD is that we are located very close to the submarine cable," Nizar said.
He said from the PAC site to the Asia Pacific Cable Network (APCN) submarine cable, the distance is only 4.6 kilometres.

"This gives a significant advantage to data centre operators in terms of connectivity," he said, adding that the overall development could take between 10 and 20 years to reach full maturity, given its scale.

APCN is an international submarine fibre-optic telecommunications cable system connecting major Asian markets, including Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea and Japan.
Nizar said that the PAC was expected to create about 12,000 employment opportunities and accommodate around 50,000 residents as the development matures.
He said the project was intended to create higher-value economic activities and employment opportunities to retain skilled Pahang-born talent in the state.
"We cannot continue to depend on Pahang's traditional industries. We cannot always rely on palm oil, low-technology manufacturing, forestry, minerals and natural resources.

"It is time for us to expand into new industries and new technologies such as these. We want highly educated Pahang children to remain in Pahang and contribute to the state's economic development," he said.
Nizar said PAC would comprise seven industry-based precincts, with four already approved while discussions remained open for the remaining three.
The four approved precincts comprise the airport, MRO, Space City and an Advanced Mobility Park.
"The seven precincts refer to the pillars of the industry. We have the airport, MRO, transit-orientated development, Space City and Advanced Mobility Park, among others," he said.

He said the remaining areas included a data centre, commercial development and a proposed free trade zone, with discussions still ongoing with the relevant authorities on policy and bonded-warehouse requirements.
Nizar said the MRO component was intended to provide additional capacity for aircraft manufacturers and operators, particularly for testing and verification activities.
He said operators in Subang currently faced limitations because of high traffic levels, which made certain testing activities difficult to conduct.
"This is why PAC is being established. The MRO area will allow manufacturers and operators to conduct testing and verification in Pahang," he said.

For the data centre component, Nizar said about 161.87 hectares had been allocated and its proximity to submarine cable infrastructure was one of the key advantages being offered to potential operators.
He said data centre operators from Europe and Hong Kong were currently conducting feasibility studies.
"Being as close as possible to the submarine cable is very important for them. That is one of the advantages we have," he said.
Nizar said the advanced mobility park would focus on emerging areas including drones, UAVs and eVTOL aircraft, forming part of the low-altitude economy.
He said the development was also intended to establish a wider space economy ecosystem, including satellite manufacturing and potential launch-related activities.

"We are introducing new industries that previously did not exist on a large scale in Pahang, such as MRO and the low-altitude economy based on drones and UAVs, as well as the orbital and space economy.

a04fe35e3c9eed15: CARACAS: Ousted former Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro's jailed wife Cilia Flores has a "very delicate" heart condition requiring surgery, Maduro's son told AFP on Monday, after Flores requested to be released on house arrest.
Flores, 69, was arrested alongside Maduro by US forces during a raid on Caracas on Jan 3 and taken to the United States to face trial on trafficking charges.
She is being held in the same federal prison in Brooklyn, New York, as Maduro.
Last month, her lawyer requested she be placed under house arrest, saying that she suffers from heart problems for which her prison conditions do not provide adequate care.
Maduro's son, Nicolas Maduro Guerra, said Flores is suffering from a "prolapsed" heart, a condition that, in rare, severe cases, can cause heart failure.
He said that she required surgery and needed to be released from prison in order to properly recuperate afterwards.
The US government has opposed her request for pre-trial release, saying she poses "an extreme risk of flight and danger to the public."
Flores' lawyer Mark Donnelly had suggested she be placed under house arrest with 24-hour armed surveillance, an electronic monitoring bracelet and that her passport be confiscated.
Maduro and his wife, who is believed to have played a key role in his regime, are accused of helping traffic cocaine into the United States, which they deny.
Maduro has asked for the charges against him to be dismissed, invoking his immunity as head of state.
After his ouster, his former deputy Delcy Rodriguez took over as interim president, with the assent of US President Donald Trump.
Rodriguez has appeared ready to comply with Trump's agenda in Venezuela, including his bid to control vast chunks of the country's huge oil reserves.
47a3be59f7a1f278: SAO PAULO, (Brazil): Flavio Bolsonaro was seen as a less charismatic version of his firebrand father, jailed former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, yet still came out on top in the first round of the election.
The right-wing senator received 47 per cent of the vote compared with 45 per cent for leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
AFP looks at the reasons behind the shock first-round lead making Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, a favorite to win the October 25 runoff.
- Household name -
Jair Bolsonaro chose his eldest son to lead the family's political project after the ex-leader was convicted of coup-plotting and barred from running for office until 2030.
Flavio Bolsonaro was a little-known senator up until that moment and had never expressed any presidential ambitions.
He essentially embraced his father's shadow on the campaign trail.
"I know I look like him. But it's hard to compare Pele's son to Pele," he said at a Rio de Janeiro rally, in reference to the world-famous football star.
"People like Flavio for his father's ideas," former farmer and migrant to Sao Paulo state Marcio Braga told AFP.

"Even with the patriarch in prison, stripped of voting rights and absent from public appearances, the Bolsonaro name still carries weight," said Marcio Malta, a political scientist and professor at the Fluminense Federal University.
The younger Bolsonaro even managed to secure more votes in the first round than his father did in the first round of his 2018 and 2022 election bids.
- 'Thirst for change' -
Around 50 per cent of Brazilians disapprove of the current Lula administration, polls show.
Rising prices and insecurity have done significant damage to the government's image throughout Brazilian society, which is highly polarized and hankering for change.
Oscarina de Oliveira, a 62-year-old caregiver, told AFP she had planned to vote for Lula, as she always has.
But "when I got there, I switched to Bolsonaro. Just to see what happens, to see if anything changes."
Lula's Workers' Party also took severe hits in Congress, with Bolsonaro's Liberal Party becoming the dominant force in both houses.
The result "didn't surprise me, because the Brazilian people have a thirst for change," said retired businesswoman Lucia Barros, 72, in Brasilia.
- 'Orange wave' -
Sunday's result is cause for celebration among right-wing forces across Latin America, already buoyed by support from US President Donald Trump.
In what has been termed an "orange wave" in reference to Trump's skin tone, not a single regional US ally in the region has lost an election since he returned to the White House last year.
Washington-aligned figures have recently taken office in Colombia, Chile and Peru, all pledging to grant freedoms they say have been repressed by the political left.
Brazil "is moving toward a similar agenda" to that of Trump's, both economically and in terms of security, Eduardo Grin of the Getulio Vargas Foundation told AFP.
Flavio Bolsonaro has styled himself as a "moderate" version of his father, an enthusiastic Trump ally.
- Corruption crisis -
A massive scandal with a disgraced banker charged with fraud at its center dominated the election campaign.
Flavio Bolsonaro's relations with Daniel Vorcaro initially caused him problems when it emerged that he had asked the banker to finance a biopic about his father.
But even Lula's campaign has conceded that Flavio Bolsonaro benefited from the scandal, which also drew in Supreme Court Judge Alexandre de Moraes, who presided over Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial.
"Let's turn the page. Enough with corruption," said 49-year-old Bolsonaro voter Eduardo Linhares.
Without the Supreme Court's recent woes, "the Bolsonaro camp's victory would have been less sweeping," said political analyst Thomas Traumann.
Experts largely agree the right-wing candidate managed to shift attention away from his own implications in the crisis to the court and to the government.
Renan Santos, a candidate eliminated in the first round, on Monday called Flavio Bolsonaro a "corrupt" man who prevailed "by relying on structural machinery and on his surname." — AFP

7797cefe84d261ea: SEMPORNA: A community-based waste management pilot in Kampung Sri Aman has collected more than 10 tonnes of household waste since March, helping prevent waste from entering the surrounding marine environment.
Led by Reef Check Malaysia (RCM) and a local community committee, the pilot provides regular waste collection services to 100 households in the water village.
RCM said the initiative was designed to shift the focus from removing marine debris to preventing waste from entering the marine environment.

The pilot, funded by Etika until the end of the year, was developed in collaboration with the Semporna District Council and district office, as well as the Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Ministry.
The programme is also generating data on household participation, waste types and quantities, and the approximate amount of waste generated per person in the water village.
Village chief Hassan Gabra said the programme showed that residents were willing to participate when provided with a clear and practical waste management system.
"Collecting more than 10 tonnes is a significant achievement for our village, but we do not want the effort to stop when the pilot ends," he said.
RCM senior programme manager (Sabah) Adzmin Fatta said the 10-tonne milestone should be viewed as more than just a measure of waste collected.
"More than 10 tonnes is not just a waste statistic. We need to ask ourselves: where would this waste have gone if the system did not exist?
"In a water village surrounded by the sea, a significant portion could eventually leak into our marine ecosystem," he said.
RCM said water villages faced particular waste management challenges due to their geography, infrastructure, accessibility and proximity to the marine environment.

It said sustained collaboration among communities, government agencies, businesses, tourism operators, civil society groups and funders would be needed to maintain the waste management system beyond the pilot period.

dfdc5ece5009399f: BOLOGNA: Italy rounded off their first chunk of Nations League fixtures with a comprehensive 3-1 win over Turkiye at the Dall'Ara Stadium in Bologna on Monday to keep their quarter-final hopes alive.

Gianluca Scamacca put the Azzurri ahead after 26 minutes only for Aral Simsir to level just after the hour. Italy hit back, though, with goals from Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito tying up the win.
Italy go second in Group A1, three points behind leaders France and one point ahead of Belgium. Turkiye prop up the table and are still looking for their first point.

Italy are rebuilding under Roberto Mancini, who has returned for a second spell as coach of a nation who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups. They beat Turkiye 4-1 in the reverse fixture on matchday 2 before drawing 1-1 with France in Paris.
The Turks went into the game underpowered with Vincenzo Montella still without several key players including the suspended Arda Guler as well as injured pair Kenan Yildiz and Hakan Calhanoglu.

After a subdued start it was the Turks who showed most promise early on with Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma having to move smartly to keep out sharp efforts in quick succession from Ozan Kabak and Salih Ozcan.

In the 26th minute, however, it was the home side who found the back of the net. Giovanni Di Lorenzo curled a cross in from the right flank, which took a little deflection before Scamacca fired the ball past Ugurcan Cakir in the Turkiye goal.
It was the Atalanta striker's second international goal after the one he scored against England three years ago.

Turkiye showed some drive early in the second half and were rewarded with an equaliser just after the hour when Zeki Celik made a fine run down the right and crossed into the box for Simsir to slam the ball home.
But parity lasted just a couple of minutes as former Bologna defender Calafiori got on the end of a free-kick to head the Italians back in front.
Esposito wrapped up the victory three minutes from time with his seventh goal in 13 games.

b230240ccbb2d8eb: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian contingent easily surpassed the six-gold target set by the National Sports Council at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games which ended on Sunday.
Their haul of nine golds, seven silvers and 16 bronzes for a total of 32 medals equalled the country's best-ever Asian Games performance at Guangzhou 2010.
Malaysia impressively finished 11th overall among 45 countries and regions at the 20th Asian Games in Achi-Nagoya.
Timesport takes a look at Malaysia's top athletes and the region's standout stars
BEST ATHLETES S. SIVASANGARI AND NG EAIN YOW (SQUASH)

Sivasangari and Eain Yow achieved what no other Malaysian squash players had done, successfully defending their Asiad singles crowns, and leading their sides to team golds. The duo also became Malaysia's first Olympic qualifiers with squash making its debut at Los Angeles 2028.
World No. 5 Sivasangari beat India's Anahat Singh for the singles title before anchoring the women's team alongside Aifa and Aira Azman to a dramatic 2-1 final win over Hong Kong.
World No. 18 Eain Yow, who won the individual gold after defeating India's Abhay Singh, subdued Pakistan's Noor Zaman in the team final to deliver Malaysia's record-equalling ninth gold overall.
BEST TEAM MEN'S SEPAK TAKRAW SQUAD
They ended a 36-year gold medal drought dating back to Beijing 1990 by toppling arch-rivals Thailand 2-0 in the team regu final.

Anchored by 34-year-old veteran Afifudin Razali in his final Asiad alongside Syahir Rosdi and Farhan Adam, the squad also won a silver in the inter-regu event to cap a historic campaign and restore Malaysia's continental supremacy.
OUTSTANDING TEAMS NATIONAL MEN'S HOCKEY TEAM
It was redemption for the Speedy Tigers who recovered from a dismal sixth-place finish in 2022 Hangzhou to capturing a silver medal in Aichi.

Playing in an emotional campaign dedicated to their former coach Sarjit Singh, who died months earlier, the Malaysia team overcame South Korea in the semi-finals before falling to defending champions India in the gold medal match.
OUTSTANDING ATHLETES
AZIZULHASNI AWANG (TRACK CYCLING)
At 38, the Pocket Rocketman capped his fifth and final Asian Games by winning the keirin gold after beating
China's Li Zhiwei apart from collecting an individual sprint bronze.
TAJ IZRIN AIMAN TAJ MADIRA (ESPORTS — GRAN TOURISMO 7)
The gamer earned the distinction of becoming Malaysia's first ever Asian Games eSports gold medal winner.
ADEOLA FAY ROBERT AND C. SHAHMALARANI (KARATE)
Debutante Adeola delivered Malaysia's first gold of the Aichi-Nagoya
Games, in the women's under-55kg, while Shahmalarani added a second gold in the women's under-50kg class.
Karate bronzes were also won by K. Thevendran (under-55kg), H. Sureeya Sankar (under-60kg) and the men's kata team.
AIDAN KHAIRUDDIN YUNUS AND CHRISTIAN DIDIER CHIN (PADEL)

The duo created history by capturing the men's doubles silver medal in padel, which was making its Asian Games debut. They had a dream run to the final before going down to Qatar's top seeded Naif brothers, Mashari and Rashed.
ELVIS PRIESTLY CLEMENT AND ENRIQUE MACCARTNEY HAROLD (DIVING)
The young Sarawakian pair claimed silver in the men's 10m platform synchro.
TAN CHEONG MIN (WUSHU)
The Malaysian contingent flagbearer earned a bronze in the nanquan and nandao, thus becoming a two-time Asiad medallist.
KHAIRULNIZAM MOHD AFFENDY (SAILING)
The four-time Olympian collected his third Asiad medal with a bronze in the men's ILCA 7 dinghy.
OUTSTANDING ASEAN ATHLETES
CARLOS YULO — THE PHILIPPINES (ARTISTIC GYMNASTICS)
The double Olympic champion dominated the apparatus finals, winning gold on the floor exercise and men's vault.
PURIPOL BOONSON — THAILAND (ATHLETICS)
The speedster smashed the Asian Games 100m record with a 9.90s run before clinching the men's 200m gold in 19.88s.
SHANTI PEREIRA — SINGAPORE (ATHLETICS)
Singapore's track star retained her continental sprint crown by winning the women's 200m gold in 22.78s.
NATIONAL RECORDS BROKEN
NURUL ALIANA SYAFIKA AZIZAN, NURUL IZZAH IZZATI ASRI AND NUR ALYSSA FARID (TRACK CYCLING — WOMEN'S TEAM SPRINT)
The women's riders broke their national record in the Asiad first round, clocking 48.023s to improve on their previous mark of 48.086s set at last year's Asian Championships.
KHIEW HOE YEAN, ARVIN SHAUN SINGH CHAHAL, LIM YIN CHUEN AND TAN KHAI ZIN (SWIMMING — MEN'S 4X200M FREESTYLE)
The quartet smashed the national record, clocking 7:18.79s to finish fifth, eclipsing the previous mark of 7:19.50s set at the 2025 SEA Games.
FATIN NURFATEHAH MAT SALLEH, AINA SYAZWANA MUHAIMIN AND IMAN AISYAH NORAZAM (ARCHERY — WOMEN'S TEAM COMPOUND)
Aina and Fatin, together with Iman, bettered their previous record of 2,075 (set at the Asia Cup in March) by shooting a total of 2,076.
SYAHMI NOR GHAZALI (WEIGHTLIFTING — MEN'S 95kg)

In his Asiad debut, Syahmi recorded a new national record. He cleared 153kg in the snatch and 200kg in the clean and jerk for a 353kg total in the new under 95kg weight class. He previously competed in the under 94kg category at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games in July, where he set a meet record of 374kg.
SPECIAL MENTIONS
PEARLY TAN-M. THINAAH (BADMINTON)
The world No. 5 pair provided the badminton camp's sole medal with bronze in the women's doubles.
YOUTH SYNCHRO DIVERS
Yong Rui Jie-Nurqayyum Nazmi (men's 3m) and Lee Yiat Qing-Ong Ker Ying (women's 3m) bagged synchro bronzes, giving hope that the future of Malaysian diving is in safe hands.
SHARUL AIMY (ARTISTIC GYMNASTICS)
He defied a torn meniscus and shoulder pain to finish eighth in the vault final in what was likely his Asiad farewell.

5971183084cec359: KUALA LUMPUR: For first-time filmmaker Jaydev Jayakumar, “Irumbuth Thottam - Ladang Besi” began close to home - literally.
Set and filmed entirely in Sri Tebong, Melaka, the 114-minute Tamil-language crime drama involved over 50 members of the local community as supporting actors and extras.

Now, after its Malaysian release on Aug 6, the film is heading overseas, with screenings planned in Australian cinemas this month through the Melbourne Malaysian Indian Cultural Club - the movie's first international outing.
According to a post on the Finas Malaysia Facebook page, "Irumbuth Thottam" will also make history by being the first Malaysian Tamil feature film to receive a public cinema release in Australia.
“Having the opportunity to bring this movie to audiences in Australia is a meaningful milestone for everyone involved,” Jaydev said in a statement.

The film follows Rahim (Irfan Zaini), a hot-headed police officer sent to the seemingly sleepy town of Sri Tebong after clashing with his superiors. There, he and his new partner are drawn into the murder investigation of a 15-year-old schoolgirl.
As the case unfolds, hidden evidence and family secrets begin to surface, gradually darkening what first appears to be a close-knit rural community.
The brooding Sri Tebong setting is central to the film’s atmosphere, with its rural landscapes shifting from warm and familiar to increasingly ominous as the investigation deepens.
Jaydev said the production was particularly personal because it allowed him to tell a story in the place he knew best, while including people from the surrounding community in the filmmaking process.
He believes the Australian screenings offer a chance to show that Malaysian filmmakers can tell distinctly local stories without limiting their audience to home.
"Irumbuth Thottam" also stars Marie Dashani Matthews, Mohana Raj, Dhurgaashini S Vijyan and Vino Shan. It has completed its run in Malaysian cinemas, earning RM238,876 at the box office.
83a873bbbcc2d1a7: PETALING JAYA: DAP berdepan dilema untuk mengekalkan sokongan teras masyarakat Cina sambil cuba menembusi kelompok pengundi Melayu menjelang PRU16, kata penganalisis.
James Chin daripada Universiti Tasmania berkata, pengundi tradisional Cina masih menyokong DAP dan memahami keperluan parti itu berkompromi sebagai sebahagian kerajaan gabungan.
Namun, katanya, kekecewaan penyokong lebih berkait dengan agenda reformasi politik yang dilihat terhenti bawah pentadbiran Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.
Katanya, pada masa sama usaha DAP menarik pengundi Melayu berdepan cabaran besar berikutan persepsi parti itu anti-Melayu dan anti-Islam yang terbentuk selama lima dekad.
“Kepimpinan DAP berjalan di atas tali yang sangat sukar antara mereka yang mahu DAP kekal dengan akar teras Cina dan pada masa sama menyedari populasi orang Cina semakin berkurang.
“Jika DAP tidak mendapat sokongan daripada komuniti Melayu atau India, parti itu akan menjadi semakin kecil pada tahun mendatang,” katanya kepada FMT.
Menurut Chin, sebahagian penyokong tegar Cina juga kurang selesa dengan usaha DAP memperluas sokongan kerana mahu parti itu kekal berasaskan masyarakat Cina.

Sementaraz itu, Syaza Shukri daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia berkata sukar bagi DAP membendung persepsi anti-Islam dalam kalangan pengundi Melayu, terutama susulan perkembangan politik selepas 2018.
Beliau menyarankan DAP memberi lebih tumpuan kepada penyampaian perkhidmatan kepada masyarakat Melayu, selain mengiktiraf kedudukan mereka sebagai majoriti.

Sebaliknya, katanya, parti itu wajar menumpukan kritikan kepada individu atau organisasi yang sengaja mencetuskan ketegangan.
“Saya faham naratif ini mungkin sukar diterima dan mungkin dituduh berkorban prinsip kesamarataan.
“Tetapi menunjukkan kefahaman adalah langkah terbaik untuk memastikan hak bukan Melayu terus terpelihara tanpa dilihat mencabar orang Melayu,” katanya.

Kelmarin, Setiausaha Agung DAP, Loke Siew Fook, dilaporkan berkata parti itu perlu membina semula sokongan di luar kelompok pengundi tradisi menjelang PRU16, sambil mempertahankan sokongan teras masyarakat Cina.
Beliau percaya DAP masih mampu memperoleh kira-kira 80% sokongan pengundi Cina berdasarkan keputusan PRN baru-baru ini, namun mengakui sukar untuk mencapai 90%.
5398242bee0ad6dd: From Terence Netto

You need not be a Rafizi Ramli enthusiast to accept that after Anwar Ibrahim vacates the role of Pakatan Harapan (PH) supremo or is obliged to do so from GE16 failure, there is no one else to take up the position.

This point is best made by former PKR youth religious leader Wan Ji Wan Hussin who in recent remarks opined that there is a void in PKR (and by extension, PH) as to who should re-take the reins of leading the movement for reform in the country.
Wan Ji held that prior to his leaving PKR last May, Rafizi provided the analytical framework and political messaging for PKR and, by implication, for PH.
He observed that Rafizi’s energy and ability to simplify complex matters equipped him for the role of standard bearer of the reformasi movement.
As the Bersama leader it will take two more general elections before he is accepted as the supremo of the reformasi movement.
He will get to that position as head of Bersama in a shorter span if he and his cohort presently avoid taking away votes which would otherwise go to PH parties in the upcoming Melaka polls.
Bersama performed poorly in their inaugural electoral foray in Johor and then wisely decided to skip the Negri Sembilan polls to re-gather their strength for a Melaka outing.
Wong Chen, the former PKR MP for Subang who has since joined Bersama, declared that the party wants to garner 12% of the vote in Melaka in comparison to the six percent it took in Johor.
This would be a negligible increase if realised and would almost certainly come from votes that would otherwise go to DAP, PKR and Amanah, the tripartite combine that composes PH.

A wiser trajectory in the prelude to GE16 which must be held by February 2028, would be for Bersama, which is actually a splinter party of PKR, to concentrate on the 10 seats (of the overall 31 seats) that PKR won in GE15.
These seats are quite easily identifiable as seats that the Rafizi cohort occupies in PKR.
Some of the occupants have already come out in support of Bersama while others presumably would wait for the dissolution of Parliament before declaring so.
This strategy is wise because Bersama would avoid incurring the resentment of PKR, DAP and Amanah in the current phase of choosing to politic without actual electoral participation.
Bersama should just wait until GE16 is announced and then go for the seats PKR won in GE15 that are held by Rafizi’s tacit supporters who are just biding their time in PKR.

It’s not that PKR does not know who these tacit supporters are. Just look at what the party leadership has recently done by allowing former PKR MPs Edmund Santhara (Segamat), Kamaruddin Jaafar (Bandar Tun Razak), and Steven Choong (Tebrau) to return to the fold.
The trio were elected in GE14 but abandoned PKR for Muhyiddin Yassin’s Bersatu in early 2020 to enable Muhyiddin to become prime minister.
That foray ended in a dead-end.
Bersama would be better off by holding to what it can reasonably hold instead of looking for what may be prospectively — but not actually — theirs.
Patience and realism are key for Bersama.
Terence Netto is a senior journalist and an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
03d55fa0940ad997: PETALING JAYA: Analysts see DAP’s struggle to maintain Chinese support while attempting to win over Malay voters as compounded by the need to dispel the perception that it is anti-Malay and anti-Islam.
Syaza Shukri of International Islamic University Malaysia said Malay voters had been repeatedly told since the 2018 general election, when Pakatan Harapan took Putrajaya, that DAP is anti-Islam.
She said DAP must emphatically recognise the Malays as the majority if it is to dispel its anti-Malay image.

"I understand this may be difficult because it feels like the rights of the non-Malays are decreasing. But the narrative must avoid blaming this on all Malays or labelling all Malays who support PAS as anti-Chinese or anti-Indian.
"The narrative must focus on individuals or organisations that stoke tensions," she told FMT.
She said the best way to ensure the rights of non-Malays are preserved would be to show that the party understands the Malays.
"I know it sounds confusing. Some might even say that’s already what DAP is about, but right now the Malay community believes that DAP wants to erode Malay rights," she said.

She was responding to DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook, who said on Sunday that the party must build support beyond its traditional base for the next general election while retaining its core Chinese support.
Loke also said the political reality in Malaysia demands consensus-building among coalition partners, and that DAP’s vision could rarely be realised in full.

James Chin of the University of Tasmania said Loke was walking a "difficult tightrope" as some wanted DAP to remain true to its Chinese roots, even as Loke was aware that the Chinese population was falling.
He said some of DAP’s "hardcore supporters" were uncomfortable with its efforts to widen its support base.
"Some of the hardcore DAP supporters are from the Chinese ground, and they do not want DAP to reach out to the Malay ground as well. They prefer DAP to be a Chinese-based party," he told FMT.
However, Chin said if DAP does not get support from the Malay or Indian communities, "it will become smaller and smaller in the coming years".
95dba282166338c7: PARIS: Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the UEFA Nations League on Monday, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge.
Dodi Lukebakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France.
But France turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in the final 13 minutes to preserve Zidane's unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals.
Desire Doue hauled France level in the 77th minute with a low drive from the edge of the area before Olise teed up Rayan Cherki to fire them ahead four minutes later.
Olise then put the result beyond doubt with a third goal before adding another in stoppage time to cap a stunning French comeback.
"Olise, what he's doing is simply exceptional," said Zidane.

France, who also beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels last week thanks to a late Olise goal, moved three points clear of Italy at the top of Group A1, with Belgium another point back. Italy beat Turkey 3-1 in Bologna to condemn their opponents to a fourth straight loss.
"It's encouraging and I'm very optimistic about what's to come," added Zidane, after wins in three of his first four matches.
"I'm pleased with the results: we have 10 points, and beyond the victories and the points, what matters most is the satisfaction of having done a good job with the players and my staff.
"It was very important to have two quality weeks. There are things we need to improve, but that will come little by little. We can do better, and we will do better."

Former World Cup and Ballon d'Or winner Zidane heavily rotated his team for the last match of this two-week long international window, with only Ousmane Dembele keeping his place among the 10 changes.
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes made their France debuts, with Dembele again captaining the side in the absence of the injured Kylian Mbappe.

Belgium were without the suspended duo of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans but caught France cold when Romeo Lavia's superb ball split open the home defence, allowing Lukebakio to race clear and tuck away a clinical finish.
Maarten Vandevoordt, making his debut in goal for Belgium, kept out efforts from Esteban Lepaul and Cherki as France pressed for an equaliser, but the dam eventually burst.

Doue gathered the ball and shot on the turn, beyond the reach of Vandevoordt, to haul France level. Cherki then turned home a cutback from Olise to give the hosts the lead as the Bayern Munich winger stole the show late on.
Olise scrambled in a third in the 88th minute and rolled in a fourth after skilful work from Doue to complete a remarkable turnaround.
